page.layout: One page of verse in italic, one block of text; running head at top; catchword "Quod" at lower right; no margin notes.

p.i:
Captúsque grandi munere mittitur
Augusta sacra limina qui domus
Perrupit audax, & retecto
Ense tuum latus appetiuit.
Hac arte Princeps concidit Auricus,
Quo dura fortes vindice vincula
Rupere Belga, quum Tyrannus
Iussit Iber violare leges,
Iurata Genti fœdera subruens.
Hæc Roma monstrat perfida, quæ fidem
Pactámque dextram Christianis
Fraude noua temerare sancit.
Cur pace s:cla, Tygride seuior,
Heu Roma quæris sub iuga mittere
Hispana bellaces Britannos,
Innocuúmque caput fatigas?
Vrit profanos fœmina Præsules
Dilecta calo, cui placet obsequi
Christo docenti: cuíque cordi est
Ardua cum pietate Virtus.
Vrit cruentis quod cruciatibus
Dulcem coactos linquere Patriam
Solatur, & Christum sequutos
Hospitiis recreat benignis.
Quòd fida sacros auxiliis greges
Firmat piorum non trepidantibus.
Longósque Belgarum labores
Marte potens miserata sanat.

page.notes: Catchword "Quod" is printed at lower right, outside the text block. Long s rendered as plain s. Page is verse; the lines are shown with line breaks inside one paragraph. Some letters in the first line ("Captúsque") and "s:cla" line are doubtful.
